Olivia — attaching the checklist and a short operations playbook excerpt. Key technical points (summary):

- Region guarantee: For Private and Dedicated, you can pin model-serving nodes to us-east-1. For Hosted, we route to the closest regional pool; you can request region pinning for higher tiers (recommended for PHI workloads).
- VPC options:
  * VPC Peering (Dedicated): Peering connection between customer VPC and Redwood serving VPC; controls for CIDR allow-listing.
  * PrivateLink (Private): Interface endpoints for control plane & optional private data plane; no public internet path from customer subnets.
  * On-prem package: offline installer and local serving option (air-gapped) for highest isolation.
- KMS/HSM: Customer-managed keys supported (AWS KMS) for model and artifact encryption at rest; options for AWS CloudHSM for FIPS 140-2 requirements.
- Egress controls & NAT: We support forced egress through customer-controlled NAT gateways or egress fences; can restrict outbound destinations via ACLs and routing policies.
- Audit & logs: Requestable audit log exports (S3) and 365/730-day retention configurable per contract.
- SOC2/SIG evidence: We maintain a SOC 2 Type II summary and can provide SIG/CAIQ responses with redacted evidence in our secure Drive link.

Attached: redwood-private-connectivity-checklist.pdf (checklist + brief playbook) and redwood-region-hosting-summary.xlsx

Regards,
Dev Patel
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
